title: Hybrid Gated-DeltaNet models exhaust Mamba cache blocks at vLLM's default max_num_seqs

symptom.error_regex: max_num_seqs \((\d+)\) exceeds available Mamba cache blocks \((\d+)\)
symptom.description: Engine core initialization fails during CUDA graph capture. The model loads and the KV cache is sized successfully first, which makes it look like a memory problem rather than a config one.

cause: Each decode sequence in a hybrid GDN model needs its own Mamba recurrent-state block. vLLM's CUDA default of max_num_seqs=1024 exceeds the number of blocks that fit alongside the weights, so CUDA graph capture cannot proceed.

fix.notes: Set max_num_seqs at or below the block count reported in the error. 256 is comfortably clear on an 80GB card and is ample for interactive/agent use. Raising gpu_memory_utilization is the alternative lever but trades away KV cache.

source: modalpi first-party: Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 on H100:1, vLLM 0.27.1, 2026-08-16 (architecture string verified against the HF API)

title: Pinning huggingface_hub alongside modern vLLM makes the image unresolvable

symptom.error_regex: No solution found when resolving dependencies|depends on huggingface-hub>=
symptom.description: Image build fails before anything runs. Common because several widely-copied Modal examples pin huggingface_hub==0.34.4.

cause: vLLM >=0.27 requires transformers >=5.5.3, which requires huggingface-hub >=1.5.0. Any pin below that is unsatisfiable.

fix.notes: Do not pin huggingface_hub at all; let vLLM resolve it. Install hf_transfer separately if fast downloads are wanted. Never copy dependency pins from an older example without re-resolving.

source: modalpi first-party: Modal image build, vLLM 0.27.1, 2026-08-16

title: Qwen3.8 emits XML tool calls, so the hermes parser silently mis-parses every call

symptom.description: No error anywhere. The server starts, requests succeed, but tool_calls comes back empty and the raw XML appears in message.content instead. Agents built on the endpoint simply never call tools.

cause: The Qwen3.8 chat template emits <tool_call><function=name><parameter=x> XML, not the JSON body that the hermes parser expects. hermes is the usual Qwen default, which makes this an easy wrong guess.

fix.notes: Verify by grepping the model's chat_template.jinja for '<function=' before choosing. qwen3_coder and qwen3_xml both map to the same parser class. This class of bug cannot be caught by a boot check - only by asserting a real tool call parses into structured tool_calls.

source: modalpi first-party: chat_template.jinja inspection + live tool-call assertion, 2026-08-16

title: vllm-metal's GDN kernel injects foreign-language garbage tokens on Apple Silicon

symptom.description: Output is fluent and correct-looking but contains occasional tokens from unrelated languages, roughly 1 per 1,100 characters. Survives top_k=20, which rules out tail sampling: the junk ranks inside the model's top 20.

cause: Defect in vllm-metal's Metal Gated-DeltaNet kernel. Same class as sgl-project/sglang#22087, which affects dense GDN models only and is explicitly not quantization-dependent.

fix.notes: No flag fixes this. Both attention paths are affected and chunked prefill does not clear it. Serve GDN models on Apple Silicon with mlx_lm.server instead, or move to CUDA. Proven by elimination: identical 4-bit weights produce 0 garbage through mlx_lm and through vLLM on an H100, and 10 through vllm-metal over comparable volume.

source: modalpi first-party: four-way A/B across vllm-metal paged, non-paged, mlx_lm, and CUDA H100, 2026-08-16

title: MXFP4 checkpoints do not load on NVIDIA devices

symptom.description: Model fails to load due to missing linear method support.

cause: vLLM has no MXFP4 linear method for NVIDIA backends.

fix.notes: Use an NVFP4 build instead on Blackwell-class hardware, or FP8 on Hopper. Check that an NVFP4 conversion of the target model actually exists before recommending it.

title: Modal's @app.server() must decorate a class with @modal.enter(), not a function

symptom.error_regex: The @app\.server\(\) decorator must be used on a class
symptom.description: Deploy aborts immediately with a TypeError, before any container starts.

cause: Published Modal vLLM examples show a function-shaped @app.server(); the 1.5.x client requires a class exposing an @modal.enter() setup method.

fix.notes: Renderer-level concern, not a spec field: the template must emit a class with @modal.enter(). Keep this entry so the diagnoser recognises the error if a user hand-edits their harness.

title: Hybrid GDN models cannot combine prefix caching with speculative decoding

symptom.error_regex: Prefix caching for hybrid GDN models .* does not support speculative decoding
symptom.description: Engine refuses to start when both are enabled.

cause: Draft-state rollback across Mamba state blocks is not implemented, so the two features are mutually exclusive.

fix.notes: Choose prefix caching over speculative decoding for agent workloads, where long prompts repeat and cache hit rates are high (measured 42.5% in a multi-turn pi session). Drop the MTP drafter model in that case.

source: modalpi first-party: vllm_metal platform.py validation + live session metrics, 2026-08-16

title: vllm/vllm-openai image has an ENTRYPOINT, so an explicit command is double-invoked

symptom.description: The container exits immediately with exit code 2. vLLM prints its top-level usage and rejects 'serve <model>' as unrecognized arguments, which reads like a bad flag rather than a duplicated invocation.

cause: The image sets ENTRYPOINT ["vllm","serve"]. A sandbox command of ["vllm","serve",...] is appended to it, so the process actually runs `vllm serve vllm serve <model> ...`.

fix.notes: Clear it with dockerfileCommands(["ENTRYPOINT []"]) before creating the sandbox, then pass the full command. Applies to any image with a baked-in ENTRYPOINT, not just vLLM's.

source: yaeger-pi first-party: Modal Sandbox via the TS SDK, vllm/vllm-openai:v0.27.1, 2026-08-16

title: MiniMax-M3 is not served by stable vLLM releases

symptom.error_regex: not a supported architecture|Model architectures \[.*MiniMaxM3.*\] are not supported
symptom.description: vLLM refuses the checkpoint at load time because the architecture is unknown to the release.

cause: M3's sparse architecture landed after the current stable vLLM release; support ships in a model-specific image rather than on PyPI.

fix.notes: Use the MiniMax-published vLLM image for M3 rather than vllm/vllm-openai, and set engine.image accordingly. Check the model card for the current tag before deploying - this entry ages quickly.

title: Multi-GPU harnesses must set --tensor-parallel-size or the model will not fit

symptom.error_regex: No available memory for the cache blocks|CUDA out of memory|does not fit
symptom.description: Reserving four GPUs and getting an out-of-memory failure looks like a sizing mistake. It is not: vLLM defaults to tensor-parallel-size 1 and tries to load the whole model onto one card, leaving the other three idle.

cause: vLLM does not infer tensor parallelism from the number of visible GPUs.

fix.notes: The renderer emits --tensor-parallel-size from hardware.count whenever it exceeds 1. Tensor parallel wants a power of two, so 2/4/8 are the usable counts.

title: Trillion-parameter checkpoints exceed a single Modal sandbox

symptom.description: There is no error - the resolver simply cannot produce a working configuration, and a naive sizer would return an 8-GPU spec that cannot possibly load the weights.

cause: One sandbox reserves at most 8 GPUs. 8xH200 is 1,128GB, and DeepSeek-V4-Pro alone is ~1,600GB at FP8 before any KV cache.

fix.notes: Refuse with the arithmetic shown rather than emitting a spec that burns GPU minutes before failing. Serve a quantised build (NVFP4 roughly halves it) or a smaller variant such as DeepSeek-V4-Flash.

source: yaeger-pi first-party: resolver sizing against real HF parameter counts, 2026-08-16
